title: MATKP Policies
bodyHtml:
Expectations For MATKP Users

Authors citing the results of analyses performed using MATKP must cite: a) MATKP, b) all external programs that collected the donors, data, or analyses underlying each dataset and their funders, and c) the relevant publication(s) underlying the results accessed via MATKP (see “How to Cite MATKP” below). 

Agreeing to these provisions is a requirement of MATKP use.

Re-using MATKP Content

Users are permitted to use figures and screenshots from MATKP in presentations and publications, with proper citation (see below).

User Tracking

The MATKP team tracks deidentified, aggregate analytics (such as hit counts for specific pages) to improve MATKP user experience. Individual user behavior is not tracked.

For MATKP Data Submitters

Want to contribute your data to a cutting-edge community resource for adipose tissue? We invite you to submit your data to our MATKP Data Registry! We are currently accepting bulk, single cell, and single nucleus RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) data. If you have any questions or are interested in submitting additional data types, please contact us at help@kp4cd.org.

Resource Distribution and Sharing

To encourage data sharing and reproducibility, we are producing open-source methods and analysis workflows. We make these freely available for use by any other parties; the code is supplied “as is” with no implied warranty or promises of support. Code should not be reused for profit or harm.

Human Transcriptomic Data Upload and Privacy Protection

Users may upload deidentified human transcriptomic data that complies with The Common Rule (45 CFR 46), HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR 160 and 164), and the NIH Genomic Data Sharing (GDS) Policy. Data may only be uploaded if they have been stripped of Protected Health Information and HIPAA identifiers. Files or content that may be re-identifiable or linked to individual identities are prohibited.

We will share the following types of transcriptomic data:

  • Aggregated, anonymized summaries and metrics derived from publicly consented data.
  • Dataset metadata descriptors (e.g., tissue type, disease state, assay platform)
  • Published data linked to publications or publicly accessible data repositories
  • Unpublished data for which the responsible authors have provided consent to data sharing

How to Cite MATKP

Users who wish to cite MATKP in a scientific publication should do so in the following format:

The Mammalian Adipose Tissue Knowledge Portal (MATKP; https://www.matkp.org), supported by NIDDK RC2 DK116691. Year Month Date of access; URL of page cited. Specific identifiers/ accession numbers for datasets used.

Users citing donors, data and/or resources collected through non-MATKP-generated studies should also cite all underlying studies comprising those datasets.

All published datasets must be cited according to the associated publication, using DOIs and PMIDs when available. Links to published studies are provided under the DOI section of each dataset visualization page on the Single Cell Browser and Differential Gene Expression Browser. Data reused from third-party repositories must adhere to their citation policies.

Access to unpublished datasets may be subject to embargoes and citation agreements (e.g., "data under review"). Users must obtain written consent from the original data providers before publicly sharing derivative works from unpublished data.

Users who cite ENRICHR pathway analyses on the Differential Gene Expression Browser should also cite the following additional references:

  • https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-14-128
  • https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkw377
  • https://doi.org/10.1002/cpz1.90

Users who cite MoTrPAC study data from endurance exercise training in young adult rats should also cite the following additional references:

  • MoTrPAC Study Group., Lead Analysts. & MoTrPAC Study Group. Temporal dynamics of the multi-omic response to endurance exercise training. Nature 629, 174–183 (2024). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06877-w
  • “The Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC). Endurance Trained Young Adult Rats Study. https://motrpac.org, https://motrpac-data.org”
